sanskrit: tathānyān api nighnantaṃ yuyudhānaṃ samantataḥ abhyadhāvad dhṛṣīkeśo vinivārayiṣus tadā
english: As Yuyudhāna went on slaying others all around him, Hṛṣīkeśa rushed up to him, wishing then to hold him back.

sanskrit: ekībhūtās tataḥ sarve kālaparyāyacoditāḥ bhojāndhakā mahārāja śaineyaṃ paryavārayan
english: Then, O great king, the Bhojas and Andhakas, all banded together and goaded on by the turning of Time, surrounded Śaineya.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā patatas tūrṇam abhikruddhāñ janārdanaḥ na cukrodha mahātejā jānan kālasya paryayam
english: Seeing them swiftly falling upon him in fury, Janārdana of great splendor did not grow wrathful, for he knew the turning of Time.

sanskrit: te tu pānamadāviṣṭāś coditāś caiva manyunā yuyudhānam athābhyaghnann ucchiṣṭair bhājanais tadā
english: But they, possessed by the frenzy of drink and driven on by rage, then struck at Yuyudhāna with the leftover drinking vessels.

sanskrit: hanyamāne tu śaineye kruddho rukmiṇinandanaḥ tadantaram upādhāvan mokṣayiṣyañ śineḥ sutam
english: As Śaineya was being struck down, the wrathful son of Rukmiṇī rushed into the fray, seeking to rescue the grandson of Śini.

sanskrit: sa bhojaiḥ saha saṃyuktaḥ sātyakiś cāndhakaiḥ saha bahutvān nihatau tatra ubhau kṛṣṇasya paśyataḥ
english: There, locked in combat — the one with the Bhojas, and Sātyaki with the Andhakas — both were slain by sheer numbers before the very eyes of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: hataṃ dṛṣṭvā tu śaineyaṃ putraṃ ca yadunandanaḥ erakāṇāṃ tadā muṣṭiṃ kopāj jagrāha keśavaḥ
english: Seeing Śaineya and his own son slain, Keśava, the delight of the Yadus, in his wrath seized then a fistful of eraka reeds.

sanskrit: tad abhūn musalaṃ ghoraṃ vajrakalpam ayomayam jaghāna tena kṛṣṇas tān ye 'sya pramukhato 'bhavan
english: That became a fearsome iron pestle, hard as a thunderbolt, and with it Kṛṣṇa struck down those who stood before him.

sanskrit: tato 'ndhakāś ca bhojāś ca śaineyā vṛṣṇayas tathā jaghnur anyonyam ākrande musalaiḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: Then the Andhakas and Bhojas, the Śaineyas and the Vṛṣṇis alike, goaded by Time, struck one another down with pestles amid the uproar.

sanskrit: yas teṣām erakāṃ kaś cij jagrāha ruṣito nṛpa vajrabhūteva sā rājann adṛśyata tadā vibho
english: Whoever among them in fury laid hold of an eraka reed, O king — that reed appeared then, O lord, as though it had become a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tṛṇaṃ ca musalībhūtam api tatra vyadṛśyata brahmadaṇḍakṛtaṃ sarvam iti tad viddhi pārthiva
english: Even a blade of grass was seen there to turn into a pestle. Know, O king, that all this was wrought by the curse of the Brahmins' rod.

sanskrit: āvidhyāvidhya te rājan prakṣipanti sma yat tṛṇam tad vajrabhūtaṃ musalaṃ vyadṛśyata tadā dṛḍham
english: Whatever blade of grass they whirled and hurled, O king, that was seen then as a hard pestle, become a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: avadhīt pitaraṃ putraḥ pitā putraṃ ca bhārata mattāḥ paripatanti sma pothayantaḥ parasparam
english: Son slew father, and father son, O Bhārata; drunken, they fell upon one another, crushing each other.

sanskrit: pataṃgā iva cāgnau te nyapatan kukurāndhakāḥ nāsīt palāyane buddhir vadhyamānasya kasya cit
english: Like moths into fire the Kukuras and Andhakas fell; in not one of them being slaughtered was there any thought of flight.

sanskrit: taṃ tu paśyan mahābāhur jānan kālasya paryayam musalaṃ samavaṣṭabhya tasthau sa madhusūdanaḥ
english: Beholding this, the mighty-armed slayer of Madhu, knowing the turning of Time, stood firm, leaning upon his pestle.

sanskrit: sāmbaṃ ca nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā cārudeṣṇaṃ ca mādhavaḥ pradyumnaṃ cāniruddhaṃ ca tataś cukrodha bhārata
english: Seeing Sāmba slain, and Cārudeṣṇa, and Pradyumna, and Aniruddha, Mādhava then grew wrathful, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gadaṃ vīkṣya śayānaṃ ca bhṛśaṃ kopasamanvitaḥ sa niḥśeṣaṃ tadā cakre śārṅgacakragadādharaḥ
english: And catching sight of Gada lying slain, the wielder of the Śārṅga bow, the discus, and the mace, filled with violent wrath, then made a clean end of them all.

sanskrit: taṃ nighnantaṃ mahātejā babhruḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ dārukaś caiva dāśārham ūcatur yan nibodha tat
english: As he of great splendor was slaying them, Babhru the conqueror of hostile cities, and Dāruka too, spoke to the Dāśārha — hear what they said.

sanskrit: bhagavan saṃhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tvayā bhūyiṣṭham acyuta rāmasya padam anviccha tatra gacchāma yatra saḥ
english: "O blessed one, O Acyuta, by you nearly all have now been destroyed. Seek out the place of Rāma; let us go there, where he is."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yayur dārukaḥ keśavaś ca; babhruś ca rāmasya padaṃ patantaḥ athāpaśyan rāmam anantavīryaṃ; vṛkṣe sthitaṃ cintayānaṃ vivikte
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Dāruka and Keśava, and Babhru too, set out, hastening, toward the place of Rāma; and they beheld Rāma of boundless valor seated beneath a tree in a solitary spot, lost in thought.

sanskrit: tataḥ samāsādya mahānubhāvaḥ; kṛṣṇas tadā dārukam anvaśāsat gatvā kurūñ śīghram imaṃ mahāntaṃ; pārthāya śaṃsasva vadhaṃ yadūnām
english: Then the great-souled Kṛṣṇa, having reached him, gave this command to Dāruka: "Go swiftly to the Kurus, and tell Pārtha of this great slaughter of the Yadus.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ kṣipram ihopayātu; śrutvā mṛtān yādavān brahmaśāpāt ity evam uktaḥ sa yayau rathena; kurūṃs tadā dāruko naṣṭacetāḥ
english: Let Arjuna come here at once, on hearing that the Yādavas have perished by the Brahmins' curse." Thus addressed, Dāruka, his senses bewildered, set off by chariot then toward the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato gate dāruke keśavo 'tha; dṛṣṭvāntike babhrum uvāca vākyam striyo bhavān rakṣatu yātu śīghraṃ; naitā hiṃsyur dasyavo vittalobhāt
english: Then, when Dāruka had gone, Keśava, seeing Babhru nearby, spoke these words: "Let your honor go quickly and guard the women, lest robbers harm them out of greed for wealth."

sanskrit: sa prasthitaḥ keśavenānuśiṣṭo; madāturo jñātivadhārditaś ca taṃ vai yāntaṃ saṃnidhau keśavasya; tvarantam ekaṃ sahasaiva babhrum brahmānuśaptam avadhīn mahad vai; kūṭonmuktaṃ musalaṃ lubdhakasya
english: He set out, instructed by Keśava, sick with drink and stricken by the slaughter of his kin; and as Babhru hurried on alone in Keśava's very presence, a great pestle — flung from the snare of a hunter and itself cursed by the Brahmins — struck him dead all at once.

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ babhrum āha; kṛṣṇo vākyaṃ bhrātaram agrajaṃ tu ihaiva tvaṃ māṃ pratīkṣasva rāma; yāvat striyo jñātivaśāḥ karomi
english: Then, seeing Babhru slain, Kṛṣṇa spoke these words to his elder brother: "Wait for me here, Rāma, while I see to the women, the wards of our kinsmen."

sanskrit: tataḥ purīṃ dvāravatīṃ praviśya; janārdanaḥ pitaraṃ prāha vākyam striyo bhavān rakṣatu naḥ samagrā; dhanaṃjayasyāgamanaṃ pratīkṣan rāmo vanānte pratipālayan mām; āste 'dyāhaṃ tena samāgamiṣye
english: Then, entering the city of Dvāravatī, Janārdana spoke these words to his father: "Let your honor guard all our women, awaiting the coming of Dhanaṃjaya. Rāma sits at the forest's edge today, waiting for me; with him shall I now unite."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaṃ mayedaṃ nidhanaṃ yadūnāṃ; rājñāṃ ca pūrvaṃ kurupuṃgavānām nāhaṃ vinā yadubhir yādavānāṃ; purīm imāṃ draṣṭum ihādya śaktaḥ
english: "I have witnessed this destruction of the Yadus, as before I witnessed that of the kings, the bulls of the Kurus. Without the Yadus I am not able today to look upon this city of the Yādavas."

sanskrit: tapaś cariṣyāmi nibodha tan me; rāmeṇa sārdhaṃ vanam abhyupetya itīdam uktvā śirasāsya pādau; saṃspṛśya kṛṣṇas tvarito jagāma
english: "I shall practice austerities — mark this from me — withdrawing to the forest together with Rāma." Having said this and touched his father's feet with his head, Kṛṣṇa departed in haste.

sanskrit: tato mahān ninadaḥ prādurāsīt; sastrīkumārasya purasya tasya athābravīt keśavaḥ saṃnivartya; śabdaṃ śrutvā yoṣitāṃ krośatīnām
english: Then a great wail arose from that city with its women and children; and Keśava, turning back when he heard the cry of the women lamenting, spoke.

sanskrit: purīm imām eṣyati savyasācī; sa vo duḥkhān mocayitā narāgryaḥ tato gatvā keśavas taṃ dadarśa; rāmaṃ vane sthitam ekaṃ vivikte
english: "Savyasācin will come to this city — that foremost of men shall free you from sorrow." Then Keśava, going on, beheld Rāma, seated alone in a solitary part of the forest.

sanskrit: athāpaśyad yogayuktasya tasya; nāgaṃ mukhān niḥsarantaṃ mahāntam śvetaṃ yayau sa tataḥ prekṣyamāṇo; mahārṇavo yena mahānubhāvaḥ
english: Then he saw a great white serpent issuing from the mouth of Rāma, who was rapt in yoga; and the noble one departed, watched by all, going toward the great ocean.

sanskrit: sahasraśīrṣaḥ parvatābhogavarṣmā; raktānanaḥ svāṃ tanuṃ tāṃ vimucya samyak ca taṃ sāgaraḥ pratyagṛhṇān; nāgā divyāḥ saritaś caiva puṇyāḥ
english: Thousand-headed, vast in girth as a mountain, red-mouthed, he cast off that body of his; and the ocean duly received him, as did the divine serpents and the holy rivers.

sanskrit: karkoṭako vāsukis takṣakaś ca; pṛthuśravā varuṇaḥ kuñjaraś ca miśrī śaṅkhaḥ kumudaḥ puṇḍarīkas; tathā nāgo dhṛtarāṣṭro mahātmā
english: Karkoṭaka and Vāsuki and Takṣaka, Pṛthuśravas, Varuṇa, and Kuñjara, Miśrī, Śaṅkha, Kumuda, and Puṇḍarīka, and likewise the great-souled serpent Dhṛtarāṣṭra —

sanskrit: hrādaḥ krāthaḥ śitikaṇṭho 'gratejās; tathā nāgau cakramandātiṣaṇḍau nāgaśreṣṭho durmukhaś cāmbarīṣaḥ; svayaṃ rājā varuṇaś cāpi rājan pratyudgamya svāgatenābhyanandaṃs; te 'pūjayaṃś cārghyapādyakriyābhiḥ
english: Hrāda, Krātha, Śitikaṇṭha of foremost splendor, and the two serpents Cakramanda and Atiṣaṇḍa, the best of serpents Durmukha, and Ambarīṣa, and King Varuṇa himself, O king — these came forth to meet him, greeted him with welcome, and honored him with offerings of arghya and water for his feet.

sanskrit: tato gate bhrātari vāsudevo; jānan sarvā gatayo divyadṛṣṭiḥ vane śūnye vicaraṃś cintayāno; bhūmau tataḥ saṃviveśāgryatejāḥ
english: Then, when his brother had departed, Vāsudeva — who with divine vision knew all the courses of things — wandering in the empty forest, deep in thought, that one of supreme splendor lay down upon the ground.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ hi tena prāk tadā vittam āsīd; gāndhāryā yad vākyam uktaḥ sa pūrvam durvāsasā pāyasocchiṣṭalipte; yac cāpy uktaṃ tac ca sasmāra kṛṣṇaḥ
english: For all of this had already been known to him beforehand: the words Gāndhārī had spoken to him long ago, and what Durvāsas had said about the spot smeared with the remnants of the milk-rice — all this Kṛṣṇa called to mind.

sanskrit: sa cintayāno 'ndhakavṛṣṇināśaṃ; kurukṣayaṃ caiva mahānubhāvaḥ mene tataḥ saṃkramaṇasya kālaṃ; tataś cakārendriyasaṃnirodham
english: Reflecting on the destruction of the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis and on the ruin of the Kurus, the noble one judged that the time of his passing-over had come; and thereupon he set about the restraint of his senses.

sanskrit: sa saṃniruddhendriyavāṅmanās tu; śiśye mahāyogam upetya kṛṣṇaḥ jarātha taṃ deśam upājagāma; lubdhas tadānīṃ mṛgalipsur ugraḥ
english: With his senses, speech, and mind reined in, Kṛṣṇa entered into the great yoga and lay still; and just then a fierce hunter named Jara, greedy for game, came to that region.

sanskrit: sa keśavaṃ yogayuktaṃ śayānaṃ; mṛgāśaṅkī lubdhakaḥ sāyakena jarāvidhyat pādatale tvarāvāṃs; taṃ cābhitas taj jighṛkṣur jagāma athāpaśyat puruṣaṃ yogayuktaṃ; pītāmbaraṃ lubdhako 'nekabāhum
english: That hunter Jara, mistaking the yoga-rapt Keśava as he lay for a deer, swiftly pierced him in the sole of the foot with an arrow; and going up to seize his quarry, the hunter beheld a man rapt in yoga, clad in yellow, with many arms.

sanskrit: matvātmānam aparāddhaṃ sa tasya; jagrāha pādau śirasā cārtarūpaḥ āśvāsayat taṃ mahātmā tadānīṃ; gacchann ūrdhvaṃ rodasī vyāpya lakṣmyā
english: Believing himself to have wronged him, stricken with grief, he clasped Kṛṣṇa's feet with his head; and the great-souled one consoled him at that moment, even as he ascended on high, filling heaven and earth with his glory.

sanskrit: divaṃ prāptaṃ vāsavo 'thāśvinau ca; rudrādityā vasavaś cātha viśve pratyudyayur munayaś cāpi siddhā; gandharvamukhyāś ca sahāpsarobhiḥ
english: As he reached the heavens, Vāsava and the Aśvins, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Viśvedevas, and the sages and the Siddhas too, and the chief Gandharvas together with the Apsarases, came forth to meet him.

sanskrit: tato rājan bhagavān ugratejā; nārāyaṇaḥ prabhavaś cāvyayaś ca yogācāryo rodasī vyāpya lakṣmyā; sthānaṃ prāpa svaṃ mahātmāprameyam
english: Then, O king, the blessed Nārāyaṇa of fierce splendor, the source of all and the imperishable, the master of yoga, filling heaven and earth with his glory, that immeasurable great soul attained to his own abode.

sanskrit: tato devair ṛṣibhiś cāpi kṛṣṇaḥ; samāgataś cāraṇaiś caiva rājan gandharvāgryair apsarobhir varābhiḥ; siddhaiḥ sādhyaiś cānataiḥ pūjyamānaḥ
english: Then Kṛṣṇa was met by the gods and the seers and the Cāraṇas, O king, and honored by the foremost Gandharvas, by lovely Apsarases, and by the Siddhas and Sādhyas bowing low.

sanskrit: te vai devāḥ pratyanandanta rājan; muniśreṣṭhā vāgbhir ānarcur īśam gandharvāś cāpy upatasthuḥ stuvantaḥ; prītyā cainaṃ puruhūto 'bhyanandat
english: Those gods welcomed him, O king; the best of sages worshipped the Lord with hymns; the Gandharvas too attended upon him, singing his praise; and Puruhūta greeted him with joy.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dāruko 'pi kurūn gatvā dṛṣṭvā pārthān mahārathān ācaṣṭa mausale vṛṣṇīn anyonyenopasaṃhṛtān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Dāruka too, having gone to the Kurus and seen the Pārthas, those great chariot-warriors, told them how the Vṛṣṇis had destroyed one another in the affray of the pestles.

sanskrit: śrutvā vinaṣṭān vārṣṇeyān sabhojakukurāndhakān pāṇḍavāḥ śokasaṃtaptā vitrastamanaso 'bhavan
english: On hearing that the Vārṣṇeyas, together with the Bhojas, Kukuras, and Andhakas, had perished, the Pāṇḍavas were consumed with grief and their minds were stricken with dismay.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunas tān āmantrya keśavasya priyaḥ sakhā prayayau mātulaṃ draṣṭuṃ nedam astīti cābravīt
english: Then Arjuna, the dear friend of Keśava, taking leave of them, set out to see his maternal uncle, saying, "This is the end of all this."

sanskrit: sa vṛṣṇinilayaṃ gatvā dārukeṇa saha prabho dadarśa dvārakāṃ vīro mṛtanāthām iva striyam
english: Going to the dwelling-place of the Vṛṣṇis together with Dāruka, the hero beheld Dvārakā, O lord, like a woman whose husband is dead.

sanskrit: yāḥ sma tā lokanāthena nāthavatyaḥ purābhavan tās tv anāthās tadā nāthaṃ pārthaṃ dṛṣṭvā vicukruśuḥ
english: Those women who once had a protector in the Lord of the world now, bereft of protection, cried aloud when they saw Pārtha as their protector.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśastrīsahasrāṇi vāsudevaparigrahaḥ tāsām āsīn mahān nādo dṛṣṭvaivārjunam āgatam
english: There were sixteen thousand women, the wives of Vāsudeva; a great wail arose from them at the very sight of Arjuna come among them.

sanskrit: tās tu dṛṣṭvaiva kauravyo bāṣpeṇa pihito 'rjunaḥ hīnāḥ kṛṣṇena putraiś ca nāśakat so 'bhivīkṣitum
english: At the mere sight of them, the Kaurava Arjuna, his eyes veiled with tears, was unable to look upon them, bereft as they were of Kṛṣṇa and of their sons.

sanskrit: tāṃ sa vṛṣṇyandhakajalāṃ hayamīnāṃ rathoḍupām vāditrarathaghoṣaughāṃ veśmatīrthamahāgrahām
english: That city, whose waters were the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, whose fish were the horses, whose boats were the chariots, whose flood of sound was the din of instruments and cars, whose great whirlpools were its mansions and bathing-ghāts —

sanskrit: ratnaśaivalasaṃghāṭāṃ vajraprākāramālinīm rathyāsrotojalāvartāṃ catvarastimitahradām
english: with gems for its rafts of waterweed, garlanded with ramparts hard as diamond, with its streets for currents and eddies of water, and its squares for still, deep pools —

sanskrit: rāmakṛṣṇamahāgrāhāṃ dvārakāsaritaṃ tadā kālapāśagrahāṃ ghorāṃ nadīṃ vaitaraṇīm iva
english: with Rāma and Kṛṣṇa for its mighty crocodiles — that river-like Dvārakā, now seized by the noose of Time, dreadful, like the river Vaitaraṇī —

sanskrit: tāṃ dadarśārjuno dhīmān vihīnāṃ vṛṣṇipuṃgavaiḥ gataśriyaṃ nirānandāṃ padminīṃ śiśire yathā
english: such did the wise Arjuna behold her, bereft of the bulls of the Vṛṣṇis, her splendor gone and her joy departed, like a lotus-pond in the cold of winter.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dvārakāṃ pārthas tāś ca kṛṣṇasya yoṣitaḥ sasvanaṃ bāṣpam utsṛjya nipapāta mahītale
english: Seeing that Dvārakā and those wives of Kṛṣṇa, Pārtha gave way to loud weeping and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: sātrājitī tataḥ satyā rukmiṇī ca viśāṃ pate abhipatya praruruduḥ parivārya dhanaṃjayam
english: Then Satyā, the daughter of Satrājit, and Rukmiṇī, O lord of peoples, ran up, and surrounding Dhanaṃjaya, they wept aloud.

sanskrit: tatas tāḥ kāñcane pīṭhe samutthāyopaveśya ca abruvantyo mahātmānaṃ parivāryopatasthire
english: Then, raising the great-souled one up and seating him upon a golden seat, they, speaking to him, stood about him in attendance.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃstūya govindaṃ kathayitvā ca pāṇḍavaḥ āśvāsya tāḥ striyaś cāpi mātulaṃ draṣṭum abhyagāt
english: Then, having praised Govinda and spoken with them, and having consoled those women too, the Pāṇḍava went on to see his maternal uncle.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ śayānaṃ mahātmānaṃ vīram ānakadundubhim putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ dadarśa kurupuṃgavaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The bull of the Kurus beheld that great-souled hero Ānakadundubhi lying down, consumed with grief for his sons.

sanskrit: tasyāśruparipūrṇākṣo vyūḍhorasko mahābhujaḥ ārtasyārtataraḥ pārthaḥ pādau jagrāha bhārata
english: More stricken than the stricken man himself, the broad-chested, mighty-armed Pārtha, his eyes brimming with tears, clasped his feet, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: samāliṅgyārjunaṃ vṛddhaḥ sa bhujābhyāṃ mahābhujaḥ rudan putrān smaran sarvān vilalāpa suvihvalaḥ bhrātṝn putrāṃś ca pautrāṃś ca dauhitrāṃś ca sakhīn api
english: The aged, mighty-armed one embraced Arjuna with both arms, and weeping, remembering all his sons, utterly overcome, he lamented — for his brothers and sons and grandsons, for his daughters' sons and his friends as well.

sanskrit: vasudeva uvāca yair jitā bhūmipālāś ca daityāś ca śataśo 'rjuna tān dṛṣṭvā neha paśyāmi jīvāmy arjuna durmaraḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: "Those by whom kings of the earth and demons were conquered by the hundreds, O Arjuna — having seen them, I see them here no longer; yet I live on, Arjuna, hard to kill that I am."

sanskrit: yau tāv arjuna śiṣyau te priyau bahumatau sadā tayor apanayāt pārtha vṛṣṇayo nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: "Those two pupils of yours, Arjuna, ever dear to you and held in high esteem — through their misconduct, O Pārtha, the Vṛṣṇis have gone to their destruction."

sanskrit: yau tau vṛṣṇipravīrāṇāṃ dvāv evātirathau matau pradyumno yuyudhānaś ca kathayan katthase ca yau
english: "Those two who alone among the foremost heroes of the Vṛṣṇis were reckoned supreme chariot-warriors — Pradyumna and Yuyudhāna — of whom you would speak in pride —"

sanskrit: nityaṃ tvaṃ kuruśārdūla kṛṣṇaś ca mama putrakaḥ tāv ubhau vṛṣṇināśasya mukham āstāṃ dhanaṃjaya
english: "of whom you, O tiger of the Kurus, and my dear son Kṛṣṇa would ever speak — those two, O Dhanaṃjaya, became the very forefront of the Vṛṣṇis' ruin."

sanskrit: na tu garhāmi śaineyaṃ hārdikyaṃ cāham arjuna akrūraṃ raukmiṇeyaṃ ca śāpo hy evātra kāraṇam
english: "Yet I do not blame Śaineya, nor Hārdikya, nor Akrūra, nor the son of Rukmiṇī, O Arjuna; for the curse alone was the cause of this."

sanskrit: keśinaṃ yas tu kaṃsaṃ ca vikramya jagataḥ prabhuḥ videhāv akarot pārtha caidyaṃ ca balagarvitam
english: "He, the Lord of the world, who by his might struck down Keśin and Kaṃsa, and who, O Pārtha, made an end of the Caidya proud of his strength —"

sanskrit: naiṣādim ekalavyaṃ ca cakre kāliṅgamāgadhān gāndhārān kāśirājaṃ ca marubhūmau ca pārthivān
english: "and Ekalavya, son of the Niṣāda, and who subdued the Kaliṅgas and Māgadhas, the Gāndhāras and the king of Kāśi, and the princes of the desert lands —"

sanskrit: prācyāṃś ca dākṣiṇātyāṃś ca pārvatīyāṃs tathā nṛpān so 'bhyupekṣitavān etam anayaṃ madhusūdanaḥ
english: "and the kings of the East and of the South and of the hill-country alike — that slayer of Madhu suffered this calamity to come to pass."

sanskrit: tataḥ putrāṃś ca pautrāṃś ca bhrātṝn atha sakhīn api śayānān nihatān dṛṣṭvā tato mām abravīd idam
english: "Then, seeing his sons and grandsons and brothers and friends lying slain, he spoke this to me:"

sanskrit: saṃprāpto 'dyāyam asyāntaḥ kulasya puruṣarṣabha āgamiṣyati bībhatsur imāṃ dvāravatīṃ purīm
english: "'Now, O bull among men, this end of our house has come. Bībhatsu will come to this city of Dvāravatī."

sanskrit: ākhyeyaṃ tasya yad vṛttaṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ vaiśasaṃ mahat sa tu śrutvā mahātejā yadūnām anayaṃ prabho āgantā kṣipram eveha na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: "'Tell him what has happened, the great slaughter of the Vṛṣṇis. He of great splendor, on hearing of the ruin of the Yadus, O lord, will come here at once — of this I have no doubt."

sanskrit: yo 'haṃ tam arjunaṃ viddhi yo 'rjunaḥ so 'ham eva tu yad brūyāt tat tathā kāryam iti budhyasva mādhava
english: "'Know that I am that Arjuna, and that Arjuna is none other than I; whatever he says, that must be done so — understand this, Mādhava."

sanskrit: sa strīṣu prāptakālaṃ vaḥ pāṇḍavo bālakeṣu ca pratipatsyati bībhatsur bhavataś caurdhvadehikam
english: "'That Pāṇḍava Bībhatsu will do what is timely for your women and your children, and will perform your funeral rites as well."

sanskrit: imāṃ ca nagarīṃ sadyaḥ pratiyāte dhanaṃjaye prākārāṭṭālakopetāṃ samudraḥ plāvayiṣyati
english: "'And this city, with its ramparts and watchtowers, the ocean will flood the moment Dhanaṃjaya has departed."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi deśe kasmiṃś cit puṇye niyamam āsthitaḥ kālaṃ kartā sadya eva rāmeṇa saha dhīmatā
english: "'For I, taking up a vow in some holy place, will at once make my end together with the wise Rāma.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā hṛṣīkeśo mām acintyaparākramaḥ hitvā māṃ bālakaiḥ sārdhaṃ diśaṃ kām apy agāt prabhuḥ
english: "Having spoken thus, Hṛṣīkeśa of inconceivable prowess, the Lord, leaving me behind with the children, departed in some direction or other."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tau ca mahātmānau cintayan bhrātarau tava ghoraṃ jñātivadhaṃ caiva na bhuñje śokakarśitaḥ
english: "And I, brooding on those two great-souled brothers of yours and on the terrible slaughter of my kin, take no food, wasted away with grief."

sanskrit: na ca bhokṣye na jīviṣye diṣṭyā prāpto 'si pāṇḍava yad uktaṃ pārtha kṛṣṇena tat sarvam akhilaṃ kuru
english: "I shall neither eat nor live on. By good fortune you have come, O Pāṇḍava. Whatever Kṛṣṇa said, O Pārtha — do all of that, every bit."
